newsitem.title: USA: US spot distillates rise, with diesel diffs mixed.
newsitem.headline: US spot distillates rise, with diesel diffs mixed.

text.p: U.S. spot heating oil, low sulphur diesel and jet fuel all rode a rallying NYMEX heat oil market, but cash markets moved in a less clear manner, with diesel differentials in New York Harbor softer, traders said.

Prompt 74-grade NYH heating oil was talked about 0.30 cent weaker at between 2.50 and 2.75 over March NYMEX heat amid signs a recent firming trend built on strength in distant California markets was tapering off.

But the same could not be said of diesel markets in Houston, where a California-related spike seemed to still be in progress, though players could not confirm any buyers dared to step up and take out an offer heard Friday morning at the rather high level of 0.50 cent over March NYMEX heat oil.

While distillate prices were benefitting from California refinery woes and short covering on the NYMEX, gasoline prices languished amid barely higher NYMEX unleaded futures and mixed to weaker differentials.

In NYH, prompt "A5" regular reformulated gasoline was heard offered about 0.25 cent weaker at 0.10 cent over March futures, while "M4" regular conventional unleaded in Houston stood unchanged at between 1.75/1.50 cents under March NYMEX.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
